SHIFT ROTATION SCHEDULE GENERATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Your rotating shift schedule, as a calendar

Pick Pitman 2-2-3, 4-on-4-off, 3-on-3-off, DuPont or 24/48, enter your crew and cycle start, and get the dates, the real hours per week and weekends off, and an .ics file for Google, Apple or Outlook. Not sure which crew you are? List a few dates you remember and the tool finds it.

Nothing is uploaded. The page makes no network calls.

Your schedule

Choose a pattern and click Show schedule.

Schedule

Yellow = day shift, blue = night shift, blank = off.

Find my crew

One date per line: 2026-10-14 D (worked a day shift), 2026-10-20 N (night shift) or 2026-10-22 - (off). More dates narrow it down.

Compare the patterns (crew A)

PatternShiftHours / weekWorst 7 daysDays off / yrWeekends off / yrLongest runLongest break

Hours per week is the cycle average. "Worst 7 days" is the most hours in any 7-day window, which is what overtime rules usually look at; check yours.

Run it from the command line

node cli.mjs --pattern pitman --crew B --anchor 2026-10-12 --days 90
node cli.mjs --pattern dupont --crew A --anchor 2026-10-12 --ics shifts.ics
node cli.mjs --compare

Get cli.mjs and rotation.mjs from the repo. Node 18+, no dependencies.

Common questions

What is a Pitman (2-2-3) schedule?

Work two days, off two, work three, off two, work two, off three, repeating every 14 days with four crews covering days and nights. It averages 42 hours a week on 12-hour shifts, gives every other weekend off and never needs more than three shifts in a row, but some weeks contain five shifts (60 hours).

How do I put a rotating shift schedule into Google or Apple Calendar?

Pick the pattern and your crew, enter the date you are on day 1 of the cycle, choose how many days to cover and download the .ics file. Import it into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook. Events use local wall-clock time, so a 07:00 shift stays at 07:00 across daylight saving changes.

I do not know which crew or cycle day I am on. What now?

Use the Find my crew box: list a few dates you remember working a day shift, a night shift or being off. The tool shows every crew position that fits. If more than one fits, add another remembered date until only one is left.

Does the tool check overtime law?

No. It reports the average hours per week and the most hours in any 7-day window, which are the numbers people ask about. Overtime rules differ by country, state, industry and agreement (for example 7(k) work periods for fire and police in the United States), so confirm with your employer or union.

Is my schedule uploaded anywhere?

No. Everything runs in this page and the calendar file is built in your browser. The page makes no network calls.

More: Pitman vs DuPont vs 4-on-4-off vs 24/48: which rotating shift pattern is best?

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. Schedules are generated from standard published patterns; your employer's roster is authoritative. This is not legal, labour or payroll advice, and overtime rules vary by jurisdiction and agreement. You are responsible for confirming your schedule with your employer before relying on it.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record. If a tool needs to survive, get cli.mjs from the repo and run it yourself.

Everything runs in your browser. The dates you enter are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors, and the tool makes no network calls. Anonymous feature events (schedule_shown, ics_downloaded, crew_fitted, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage and can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

Related tools: Volunteer Shift Scheduler and Shift Roster Builder.

Free and open source. If this saved you an afternoon, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.

← Shift Rotation Schedule Generator

Which rotating shift pattern is best?

There is no best pattern, only the one whose trade-offs suit the work and the people. The numbers below are computed from the patterns themselves (crew A, 12-hour shifts except the fire-service patterns), so you can compare like with like before a roster change is proposed or accepted.

PatternHours / weekMost in any 7 daysDays off / yrFull weekends off / yrLongest runLongest break
2-2-3 (Pitman)42601832633
4-on-4-off42481832044
3-on-3-off42481831733
DuPont (28-day)42721832647
24 on / 48 off56722431712
48 on / 96 off56722432624

What the numbers say

  • All the 12-hour patterns average 42 hours a week and 183 days off. The difference is how those days are arranged, not how many there are.
  • Pitman never has more than three shifts in a row and gives every other weekend off, but a 3-shift block and a 2-shift block either side of a short break make a 5-shift (60-hour) week. It is popular because the breaks are short and frequent.
  • 4-on-4-off has the gentlest worst week (4 shifts, 48 hours) but fewer full weekends off, and a four-night block is a long run to stay alert through.
  • DuPont has the longest break, seven days every four weeks, paid for with a 6-shifts-in-7-days stretch (72 hours) when it switches between days and nights.
  • 24/48 and 48/96 have the most days off, and the highest hours on the clock, which is why fire services treat their hours differently from 12-hour shift work.

Questions to ask before you switch

  1. What is the worst 7-day stretch, and how is overtime defined for it where you work?
  2. How many consecutive night shifts, and how long to recover after them?
  3. Do the same people end up on weekends, holidays or the night crew forever?
  4. How does handover work when a crew changes mid-pattern?

Using the generator

Choose your pattern in the tool, see your crew's calendar and download it as a calendar file. If you do not know which crew you are, enter a few dates you remember working and it finds the crew and cycle day for you.

No warranty. Provided free and as-is. General information about shift patterns, not professional advice, and not legal, labour or payroll advice; overtime and rest-period rules differ by jurisdiction and agreement. Best-effort hosting, no SLA. The page makes no network calls and uploads nothing. Generate a schedule.
